## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ariyarūpakathā* (Kv 14.4) is an Abhidhamma debate belonging to the fourteenth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*. The controversy addresses the proposition, attributed to the Andhaka school, that the bodily action and speech of the Ariyans constitute noble matter (*ariyarūpa*) [Dube 1980]. S. N. Dube observes that this view belongs to a wider doctrinal tendency seeking to invest material form (*rūpa*) with moral status, causal conditions, and results, prompted both by the notion that the law of kamma is ubiquitous and by the consideration that physical speech and bodily deeds, though materially constituted, possess moral character [Dube 1980].

 It identifies no curated cross-canonical parallels.
